body.theme: Dead caps and fail-open accounting in the CI layer
body.text: The workflow layer that runs the whole laboratory has a dead daily cap (CHAIN_CAP unreachable through per_page=100), a path filter that leaves four subsystems' tests untriggered, and four fail-open paths that silently skip budget/accounting checks on transient errors. None of these are visible from a green Actions run; they were found only by reading the YAML line by line.

body.theme: The queue state machine has states without automated exits
body.text: The item state machine is explicit and well-guarded on the paths the worker drives, but the states reached by hand edits, chat claims, withheld gates and crashed runs have no exit: a stuck item (Q58), two 30-hour-old chat claims blocking ten items, and un-re-gateable split items are all live at the branch tip. Every reservation leak and evidence-free escalated item traces to one of these unreachable-exit states.

body.theme: Fail-open gates around model and network failures
body.text: A repo whose design philosophy is fail-closed has a second family of gates that fail open when the infrastructure under them errors: a gh API failure turns the code-merge gate vacuous, a missing key aborts the fallback chain instead of trying the next pool, a failed log fetch files evidence-free bugs, and pick() is blind to pending reservations. Each is a small try/except away from the design intent.

body.theme: The runner dropped the loop's measurement-integrity guards
body.text: run.py - the tool that scored all 245 proposals - accepts the counter's exit-1 (non-deterministic) signal, never cross-checks the counted run's output against the native run, and headlines exactly the marginal metrics loop.py's schema labels 'gameable ... never use it to decide'. loop.py already implements every one of these guards; they were not ported, and no test would notice.

body.theme: The trust layer's residual soft spots
body.text: The ledger's chain construction and the four committed anchors verify cleanly (recomputed at this commit), but the pieces around them trust unverified metadata (bundle integratedTime), report explorer lag as forgery, are not crash-atomic, and - the monitor excepted nowhere - the strongest anti-rewrite check runs in no workflow and has no test.

body.theme: Documentation drift is systematic, not incidental
body.text: Seventeen findings are stale numbers or stale claims: README/VERIFY/subsystem cards off by 2-4x on test counts and line counts, a leaderboard 2.4x behind its branch, a plan-2 speedup range that does not match its own committed scoreboards, and two exit-code contracts that are unreachable. The repo's own weekly indicators catch some of this; nothing regenerates the numbers automatically.

body.theme: Pre-registration discipline leaks at the edges
body.text: The project pre-registers its benches and plans, and the benches honour their registrations; but the transfer study's amendment check is advisory-only, the P5 confirm rule as implemented is stricter than the registered rule, and the leaderboard decides on the marginal metrics the plan's own schema warns against. The discipline exists; the enforcement between registration and code has gaps.

body.theme: Test coverage is thin exactly on the security-critical paths
body.text: Eleven findings are coverage gaps: the runner's gates, the monitor, the counter's jail modes, scale's real path, and three whole subsystem suites have no automated invocation - and three test files silently skip most of their tests when run directly. The repo's test suite is strong where it exists; it does not exist where this review found the worst defects.

body.theme: The repo's own external review was right, and its fixes are incomplete at the edges
body.text: The Gemini-20261120 round fixed F009/F010/F002/F011/F012 as claimed (verified in the diff), but two of the five claimed reproduction tests do not exist, the per-call paid permission left ROUTER_ALLOW_PAID as a global escape, the paid log relabelling misses the usage log, and the verdict gate now escalates on malformed replies instead of retrying. Fixing under review pressure left the last mile open.

body.theme: The scheduler dependency is the root cause of the orchestration debt
body.text: GitHub's free cron is the lab's weakest infrastructure - the repo measured 3 firings in 30 hours - and every workaround (self-chaining with a dead cap, keepers sleeping on runners, 30-minute idle re-polls, propose chains on unpushed state) is compensation with its own failure modes. A reliable trigger would retire half this list.
